scene_templates.name: Hook hero in motion
scene_templates.use_when: First 2-6 s of every video. The claim must be visible before it is explained.
scene_templates.layout: Hero object in the stage band (y 25-70%), caption in the top band, bottom band empty (no presenter yet). Optional honesty disclaimer at lower-left from frame 0.
motion_beats: Frame 0: object already moving (whip-in, pour, slide or fade completes within 12 frames @30)
0.5-1.2 s: first label, badge or callout pops
1.2-2.5 s: the transformation (shatter, morph, race result, wave flattening)
By 3 s: result state is on screen and the gap is open
Hand over to the presenter entry on the next sentence
sfx: whoosh on the transformation (the loudest hit of the opening)

scene_templates.name: Hero object + leader-line callouts
scene_templates.use_when: Naming the parts of a physical thing; any time a new object becomes the subject.
scene_templates.layout: Object centred in the stage band at 45-80% of frame width; tracked-caps labels left or right with thin leader lines; footnote lower-left; presenter bottom.
motion_beats: Object pops or slides in (8-12 frames @30)
Leader line draws on (6-10 frames)
Label fades in 4-5 frames after its line
Next callout staggers 6-8 frames later, one per spoken part
Optional single sheen sweep across the object
sfx: soft pop or beep per label

scene_templates.name: Persistent metaphor stage with state swaps
scene_templates.use_when: The core explanation. One object or metaphor must hold a mental model for 5-25 s (longer if split by overlays).
scene_templates.layout: Stage object fills y 28-70% (desk, map, rack, tile field, cross-section, keyboard). A measuring device is built into it (ruler, readout, counter). Callouts and a legend at the left.
layers: Items or tokens placed on it
motion_beats: One change per spoken noun, every 1-1.5 s
Each idea is a three-state swap on the same object: neutral, broken (red, grey, '?'), fixed (green, glow)
Non-focused groups dim to about 30%
The embedded gauge updates with every item and changes hue at thresholds
Reset to neutral before a second pass (new algorithm, new input)
sfx: pop or click per item landing
low impact on a failed state
click when a frame or lock lands

scene_templates.name: Macro zoom or zoom-through into a part
scene_templates.use_when: The story changes scale: into a component, down to a cell, or back out to thousands.
scene_templates.layout: Stage scales 2.8-8x toward the part; macro artwork fills the stage band; one label; 'magnified illustration' footnote. Captions and presenter stay locked.
layers: ZoomStack: wide art, then L2 macro art
motion_beats: Push over 20-35 frames @30 (or a 5-8 frame punch)
Blur peaks mid-move; artwork tier swaps at the peak
Soft settle, then one label
Hold 0.6-1.5 s while internals animate
Return by reverse pull-out or continue into the next scene
sfx: click or soft impact on landing

scene_templates.name: Big number or odometer with unit
scene_templates.use_when: A spoken figure is the point of the sentence.
scene_templates.layout: Numeral at 7-14% of frame height at the top or side of the stage; small unit label under or beside; optional tick bar or scale; proof card or dimmed stage beneath; source footnote.
motion_beats: Count-up over 20-45 frames @30, easing out and landing on the spoken word
The roll passes through plausible intermediate values
Unit pops; footnote fades in 0.5-1 s later
Hold, then the number shrinks into a corner stat or thumbnail
sfx: riser before the biggest number of the video

scene_templates.name: Side-by-side or before-after compare
scene_templates.use_when: Two things must be judged against each other: old vs new, theirs vs yours, input A vs input B on the same rig.
scene_templates.layout: Two columns (or two stacked rows), each with object, name and value. A winner marker, operator glyph or ratio stamp sits between or above.
motion_beats: A slides in; B follows 15-30 frames @30 later
Counters or bars race
Winner turns green; loser turns red or dims
Marker hops to the winner (10-12 frames, squash on landing)
Ratio stamp pops, tilted about -8 degrees
sfx: chime or impact on the stamp

scene_templates.name: Evidence card: document or real UI in a frame
scene_templates.use_when: A claim needs a receipt: a quote, spec line, paper, release note or app screen.
scene_templates.layout: Rounded card in y 45-72% (or centred over a dimmed stage) with header bar, body text and a source tag. Hero object may stay above it.
layers: Card with header bar and body
motion_beats: Card springs up or blurs in (8-10 frames @30)
Internal scroll to the line with vertical blur (8 frames)
Highlighter wipes from the left (8-10 frames)
Optional: other lines dim to 30%, the line lifts out as a chip
Card exits by slide or blur
sfx: ding on a date or name

scene_templates.name: Device with live screen + side meter
scene_templates.use_when: Showing load, progress or failure on a product the viewer owns.
scene_templates.layout: Front-on device centred; vertical pill meter in a narrow side column; magnified chrome strip floating above the screen.
motion_beats: A step every 1-1.5 s adds an item (pop, 8 frames @30)
Meter springs to the new fill; hue changes at thresholds
Failure: screen desaturates, spinner mounts, red glow behind the meter
Optional cross-fade of the deck to an x-ray
sfx: beep per meter step, rising in pitch (ours)
low thud on the red state

scene_templates.name: Exploded view, x-ray reveal or layer peel
scene_templates.use_when: The inside of an object, or its stack of layers, is the explanation.
scene_templates.layout: Object centred; layers separate vertically or peel away; internals labelled one per second.
motion_beats: Layers spring apart (12-20 frames @30) or peel 15 frames each
Opaque-to-glass material cross-fade (about 10 frames)
Sequential fills and labels, one per second
Collapse back to the solid object

scene_templates.name: Flow or node-wire diagram with travelling packets
scene_templates.use_when: Something moves between parts: requests, data, sound, current, couriers.
scene_templates.layout: Source node at left or top, targets at right or bottom, 2-5 paths between; optional container frame around a group; labels at the ends.
motion_beats: Wires draw on (12-18 frames @30, staggered 6)
Packets loop along the paths (15-30 frames per trip)
A state change recolours the wire (accent to grey or to green)
Container frame draws on while the layout reflows
Targets resolve with check pops

scene_templates.name: Chart build: line, bars or timeline
scene_templates.use_when: A trend, ranking or span of time; keep to two or three series.
scene_templates.layout: Minimal axes in the stage band; value label rides the head of the line or the end of the bar; source footnote under the chart.
motion_beats: Line draws on (30-90 frames @30) with a counter tied to its head
Bars grow (12-45 frames) with a synced count-up
Markers and ticks drop in (4-6 frames)
Abnormal part recolours (red spike, hatched shortfall)
Stamp or bracket pops last
sfx: tick rising in pitch under the draw (ours)

scene_templates.name: Unit grid: quantity as a picture
scene_templates.use_when: A count or a share is easier to see than to read.
scene_templates.layout: Grid of tiles, icons or thumbnails in the stage band; live counter above or below; optional legend.
motion_beats: Items fly in or flip with a 1-frame stagger (20-45 frames @30 in total)
Counter equals the number of lit items
A subset recolours to show the share
Optional collapse of the previous scene into one tile

scene_templates.name: Dimmed-stage overlay or pop-forward detail card
scene_templates.use_when: One detail or one comparison must be read without leaving the main diagram.
scene_templates.layout: Stage drops to 15-30% opacity with 9-15 px blur; overlay card or data rows on the centre axis.
motion_beats: Dim in 6-8 frames @30
Element scales 1 to about 1.6 and moves to centre (12 frames)
Content types, flips or counts
Stamp lands
Element shrinks and docks; stage restores to 100%

scene_templates.name: Chapter card + progress rail
scene_templates.use_when: The video has 3-5 named steps. Ours: every video over 60 s.
scene_templates.layout: Roadmap (map, rail or tokenised header) at y 27-31% or filling the stage for the card; active node lit; corner stat slot at the right end.
layers: Rail or roadmap with N nodes
motion_beats: Nodes light in sequence, 4-5 frames @30 apart
Active node pulses (12 frames)
Finished nodes turn green
Big numbers shrink into the corner stat after their beat
scene_templates.frequency: 3/12 videos; card repeats 4-5 times, rail persists

scene_templates.name: Terminal or typed input
scene_templates.use_when: A command, search or keyword is the action.
scene_templates.layout: Mono line under a title row inside a dark card; one token highlighted; result appears below.
motion_beats: Type 1-2 frames @30 per character
Caret blinks on a 15-frame cycle
One flag or token gets a highlight
Result card springs in

scene_templates.name: Shrink-to-thumbnail carry-over
scene_templates.use_when: A section ends but its diagram will be compared against later.
scene_templates.layout: Old diagram scales to 20-25% and parks in a top or bottom corner; new hero takes the stage.
layers: Thumbnail of the previous diagram (may dim to 25%)
motion_beats: Scale and translate to the corner in 10-14 frames @30
Thumbnail stays as a breadcrumb for 5-40 s
Callback label lands on the spoken comparison

scene_templates.name: Recap accordion or checklist
scene_templates.use_when: Before the twist or the CTA: restate the steps in one sentence.
scene_templates.layout: 3-4 rows on a left spine; the active row expands to a miniature of its scene or fills its check circle.
motion_beats: One row per clause, about 1.7 s each
Row height springs open (10-12 frames @30)
Check pops (5-6 frames)

scene_templates.name: Acted-out social CTA
scene_templates.use_when: The last 1.2-6 s. The ask is performed, not written on a card.
scene_templates.layout: Previous scene scales down, dims or is trapped in a phone; a UI card (follow chip, share sheet, comment sheet, DM thread) sits at y 28-72%; cursor on top.
motion_beats: Card slides up (10-12 frames @30)
Cursor moves (10-12 frames) and presses (3-frame squash)
State flips in 4-6 frames ('Follow' to 'Following', 'Send' to 'Sent')
Final state holds to the last frame (ours: at least 0.5 s)

easings.in_out: cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1) - camera pushes, stroke traces, flips
easings.in: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1) - exits and the first half of a zoom-through
easings.linear: loops, typewriter, scan lines, packets, dissolves, idle drift
easings.note: curves are estimates; the dossiers could not measure easing

springs.note: guesses tuned to the overshoot the dossiers describe; their 'damping 12-14, stiffness 180' pair would overshoot 15-21%

overshoot.rule: overshoot only on small elements; never on camera moves or captions

roles.item_lands_on_stage: click or pop, pitch rising as the stage fills
roles.zoom_through: whoosh plus low impact on landing
roles.chapter_change: riser 0.5-1 s before, impact on landing

bpm.reference: undetected in 10 of 12; 90.9 in one; about 48 (possibly half-time of about 97) in one

music.mood: low, steady, even-energy bed that sits behind the voice; reference keys are C# major (7), D# minor (3), E minor (2); ours adds a lift at each act change and at the CTA

loudness_lufs.note: targets are recommendations; the dossiers measured SFX at about -42 to -13 dB and did not measure programme loudness

sound_profile.beat_sync: voice-led: captions and visual events follow word timestamps; only chapter changes and the 2-3 biggest reveals snap to bar lines

quality_gates: Render is 1080x1920 at 60 fps and every animation is driven by the frame number (no CSS transitions or wall-clock timers).
Something is moving on frame 0 and the first caption word is visible by 0.2 s.
The stage shows at least 3 distinct visual states within the first 3.0 s.
No logo, intro card or greeting before the hook claim.
The hook's claim is demonstrated visually before 7 s.
Average visual beat rate is 0.7-1.2 changes per second across the video.
No span longer than 1.5 s without a visible change on the stage; payoff holds of up to 0.7 s keep ambient motion or drift.
Every scene change keeps at least 2 of the 3 bands (caption, stage, presenter) continuous.
Hard cuts are at most 1 per 30 s, and each one has caption and presenter running through plus a blur-in on the new hero.
Every zoom-through swaps artwork at the blur peak; no L0 art is ever scaled above 1.5x.
One ISO angle is used for all 3D objects in the video; flat modes are only PLAN, ELEVATION or CARD.
No outline strokes on solid objects; strokes appear only on annotations and x-ray shells.
Every 3D box uses the theme's three face tones with light from the top-left.
The presenter is absent during the hook, enters by 7 s and is visible for at least 80% of the runtime.
The presenter changes pose on phrase boundaries, at least once every 4 s and on average every 1-2 s.
No presenter pose change is a hard swap; each is a sprung move of 12-16 frames @60.
The presenter never overlaps data, labels or footnotes.
Caption words appear 2-5 frames @60 before their audio onset.
Captions never exceed 2 lines or 4 words per phrase, and stay inside y 15-25% and x 18-82%.
At most one highlight box per phrase, and only on a number, a proper noun or the contrast word.
No label is smaller than 30 px and no footnote smaller than 22 px.
No moment shows more than the caption plus two labels (footnote excluded).
Every spoken number has an on-screen readout that animates and lands within 2 frames @60 of the spoken word.
Every number carries a unit, and every sourced figure has a footnote on screen for at least 1.5 s.
Each accent colour has exactly one meaning in the video's accentMap, and every state is shown by colour plus an icon or motion.
The presenter's brand colour is not used for any state or data element.
At least one honesty element is present: an 'illustration' disclaimer, a stated limit or a caveat section.
Any open loop planted in the first 15 s is closed on screen before the CTA.
The payoff reuses the hook object or composition.
Narration runs at 195-205 wpm and each payoff is followed by a 24-40 frame @60 hold with no new text.
Each technical term is introduced after its picture and glossed in the same sentence.
SFX density is 4-6 events per 10 s with no gap longer than 8 s.
Every count-up, stamp, chapter change and cursor press has a mapped sound.
Master loudness is -14 LUFS integrated (plus or minus 1) with true peak at or below -1 dBTP, and music sits at least 15 dB under the voice.
The CTA is acted out as UI in 1.2-6 s and the final state holds for at least 0.5 s.
Videos longer than 60 s show a persistent progress rail or scoreboard.
No creator name, handle, mascot likeness, third-party logo or screenshot appears; all artwork is original vector.
